title: Tencent WeLM-Image: 31.7B Open Model With Dual-Path MoT
summary: Tencent releases WeLM-Image, a 31.7B-parameter open-source model using dual-path MoT architecture for unified image generation and editing tasks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Tencent WeChat Vision launched WeLM-Image, a 31.7B-parameter open-source model with dual-path Mixture-of-Transformers architecture activating 5.4B generation parameters per token.
- The model unifies text-to-image synthesis, instruction-guided editing across 27 action types, and multi-reference composition in one backbone designed for single-GPU deployment.
- A distilled WeLM-Image-Turbo variant renders 1024x1024 images in under five seconds on NVIDIA H20 hardware using eight guidance-free inference steps.


Tencent's WeChat Vision team officially launched WeLM-Image on November 6, 2026, a 31.7-billion-parameter image model that uses a dual-path Mixture-of-Transformers architecture to unify text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. The model activates approximately 5.4 billion parameters per target latent token during generation, while a distilled Turbo variant renders 1024x1024 images in 4.98 seconds on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially released on November 6, 2026, WeLM-Image arrives as an[open-source model](https://emergent.sh/glossary/open-source-model) designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications. The accompanying research paper, titled "WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence," details the architecture and benchmark results. Tencent positions the release as part of a sustained push in Chinese generative AI, with 355 related stories logged in the past 90 days across the ecosystem.


## Dual-Path Mixture-of-Transformers Architecture


WeLM-Image implements a dual-path Mixture-of-Transformers backbone that separates understanding and generation tasks to reduce optimization interference. The understanding path activates 2.2 billion parameters, while the generation path activates 5.4 billion parameters. Each path incorporates 64 routed experts per layer, creating a sparse Mixture-of-Experts structure within the larger 31.7-billion-parameter total. The authors write that shared attention layers connect both paths while independent parameters handle task-specific processing.


This architectural split enables the model to handle 27 distinct edit action types spanning object manipulation, background alterations, portrait adjustments, and restoration workflows. The unified backbone consolidates text-to-image synthesis, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference composition into a single deployable artifact rather than requiring separate specialized models for each task.


## Benchmark Performance and Evaluation


At 1536-pixel resolution, WeLM-Image ranks first among evaluated open-source models on three benchmarks: PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench. The research paper does not publish per-benchmark numerical scores or include closed-source model comparisons in the evaluation set. The authors emphasize the model's performance within the open-source category, positioning it as a leading option for developers requiring permissive licensing and on-premise deployment.


## WeLM-Image-Turbo: Distilled Inference Speed


The WeLM-Image-Turbo variant achieves 1024x1024 image rendering in 4.98 seconds on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU using an eight-step distillation process with guidance-free inference. This distillation reduces the full model's parameter activation overhead while preserving output quality for latency-sensitive applications. The Turbo configuration targets real-time and near-real-time use cases within consumer-facing products, where sub-five-second generation latency meets user experience requirements for interactive workflows.


## What This Means


WeLM-Image demonstrates Tencent's strategy of building unified, efficient architectures optimized for deployment at scale rather than pursuing maximum parameter counts or closed-ecosystem lock-in. The dual-path MoT design addresses a common bottleneck in multi-task models, where shared parameters often degrade task-specific performance. By open-sourcing a 31.7-billion-parameter model that runs on single-GPU configurations, Tencent lowers the barrier for enterprises and developers seeking competitive image generation without cloud API dependencies or proprietary licensing constraints.
